newsitem.title: USA: N.J. leading index at 1.5 in February, Pa. at 0.8.
newsitem.headline: N.J. leading index at 1.5 in February, Pa. at 0.8.

text.p: The Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia said Wednesday its leading index for New Jersey was 1.5 in February, its highest level in nine months.
The Philadelphia Fed said its leading index for Pennsylvania was 0.8 in February.
The bank said the New Jersey index suggests the state's expansion should continue at least through the end of this year.
The U.S. leading index is constructed using a different method and is not strictly comparable to the state indexes.
The leading index is essentially a nine-month forecast of the growth of the state's current economic activity index, also published by the Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia.
A positive reading signals growth over the next nine months, and a negative reading signals a decline.
